'''Jürgen Gauß''' (Juergen Gauss) is a German [[theoretical chemist]].

Gauß was born on 13 August 1960 in [[Konstanz]]. He studied chemistry at the [[University of Cologne]] from 1979 till 1984. After finishing his PhD thesis on abinitio calculations at the [[University of Cologne]] in 1988, he did postdoctoral studies at the [[University of Washington]] in [[Seattle]] and at the [[University of Florida]] in [[Gainesville, Florida|Gainesville]] about quantum theory. He did his [[habilitation]] in 1994 at the [[University of Karlsruhe]] on [[Computational chemistry|abinitio calculations]] of [[Chemical shift|NMR-shift]]s. In 1995, he became professor at the [[University of Mainz]].

In 2005, he received the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]], which is the highest honour awarded in [[Germany|German]] research.
